major_concerns: Validator (Batfish) coverage and false negatives may bias safety estimates toward optimistic outcomes.
Adversarial prompt corpus design may not represent real-world attack diversity; results sensitive to prompt construction.
Repair-loop behavior depends on LLM prompt engineering and may be sensitive to hidden model updates (hosted API drift).
Simulator/vendor mismatch: Batfish/sandbox may not reflect multi-vendor production behaviors.
required_design_repairs: Explicitly preregister and document Batfish coverage matrix and known gaps; include tests to quantify validator false-negative rate (oracle or human spot-checks).
Broaden and justify adversarial prompt-generation methodology; include red-team diversity metrics and seed list for reproducibility.
Preregister exact model versions/IDs, prompt templates, and retry policy; log model API responses and provider metadata (timestamps, model identifier).
Include sensitivity analysis across topology complexity and at least synthetic multi-vendor config variants; report limits of generalization in preregistration.

major_concerns: Human-approval baseline is modeled (simulated latency) — modeling choices can drive apparent time benefits and threaten causal claims.
Automated rollback success observed in simulator may not transfer to real deployments (external validity).
Canary sizing, health-check definitions, and rollback triggers are design choices that materially affect outcomes and could be tuned post hoc.
Ethical/operational extrapolation risk if readers infer production readiness from simulated gains.
required_design_repairs: Preregister the human-approval latency distribution, justify choices, and run sensitivity analyses across plausible latency families.
Preregister canary size, health-check definitions, rollback-trigger thresholds, and include rationale; conduct subgroup analyses by these parameters.
Include a realism validation step: compare simulator rollback behavior against a small set of more realistic scenarios or documented operator traces if available.
Limit claims to sandboxed evidence and explicitly report inability to claim production generalizability; add concrete threats-to-validity text in preregistration.

major_concerns: Retrieval-index composition/quality may drive observed RAG gains (confounder) unless fully specified and varied.
Automated heuristics for detecting hallucination-driven misconfigurations risk mislabeling complex but legitimate constructs.
Prompt templates and retrieval-conditioning instructions may overfit to particular attack styles; generality unclear.
required_design_repairs: Preregister and publish retrieval corpus and indexing parameters; evaluate results under at least two differently constructed indices (e.g., clean authoritative vs noisy).
Define and validate hallucination-detection heuristics with human adjudication on a stratified sample; report precision/recall of heuristics.
Preregister prompt templates and retrieval prompts; include robustness checks across prompt variations and retrieval-quality strata.
Log retrieved documents per run and report retrieval relevance scores in analysis.

major_concerns: Workflow-submetric definitions are subjective and may be dataset-specific; risk of overfitting to the corpus used to derive them.
Observed correlations do not imply causation; predictive performance may not translate to prescriptive or operational utility.
Sandbox executability score may poorly reflect production executability; scoring thresholds may be arbitrary without external validation.
required_design_repairs: Provide precise, formal definitions and computation procedures for each submetric and preregister them (include edge-case rules).
Include an external holdout or cross-dataset validation set to assess generalization; if possible, hold out a vendor or topology class for validation.
Distinguish predictive claims from causal claims explicitly; if claiming prescriptive use, add controlled intervention evaluation or simulation of decision-making using the score.
Report inter-rater reliability if any human labeling is used for trace quality; preregister ablation and threshold-selection procedures.
